title: pt2 PyTorch models must be validated before torch.export.load when pickle deserialization is disabled
answers: loading a pytorch pt2 model with MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false runs code from the archive
pt2 model load refused when pickle is disallowed
pytorch export model arbitrary code execution on load
why does mlflow.pytorch.load_model reject my pt2 model with pickle disabled
body:
Symptom: with MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false, a PyTorch model saved with serialization_format='pt2' could execute code embedded in a crafted .pt2 archive on load, even though the eager (torch.load) path was guarded.
Root cause: mlflow/pytorch/__init__.py:_load_by_pickle_check guarded only the eager torch.load branch. The pt2 branch passed the archive to torch.export.load, which unpickles sample inputs, weights and constants with weights_only=False.
Fix pattern: when _is_pickle_deserialization_allowed() is false, call _validate_pt2_archive_is_pickle_free(model_path) before torch.export.load. It accepts only short text metadata, JSON records, raw tensor records marked use_pickle: false (_pt2_raw_tensor_records), and records that pass torch.load(weights_only=True). Any other record raises MlflowException naming it.
Constraints: skipped when pickle is allowed, in Databricks Runtime or in Model Serving; the flag defaults to true. Below torch 2.10 the validator refuses instead of validating.
applies: Any change to how the pytorch flavor loads pt2 archives or to the pickle guard in mlflow/pytorch/__init__.py.
says: Disabling unsafe model deserialization still allows exported PyTorch models to run embedded malicious code.
Loading an exported PyTorch model gets rejected when unsafe deserialization is turned off.
Ensure exported model packages are inspected for unsafe code before opening them safely.
Opening exported models fails with validation errors on older supported framework versions.
Safely load tensor weights and metadata from exported models when blocking code execution.
search: When MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false, mlflow/pytorch/__init__.py:_validate_pt2_archive_is_pickle_free must validate pt2 archives before torch.export.load because _load_by_pickle_check guarded only eager torch.load. torch.export.load unpickles sample inputs, weights, and constants with weights_only=False, allowing code execution in crafted archives. The validator accepts short text metadata, JSON records, raw tensor records with use_pickle: false (_pt2_raw_tensor_records), and records passing torch.load(weights_only=True), raising MlflowException on others. Skipped when pickle is allowed (the default), in Databricks Runtime, or in Model Serving, and refused below PyTorch 2.10.
